sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是《99%隐形》。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: In February of 2021, at around 9.40 p.m.,
sentences.zh: 2021年2月，晚上9点40分左右，

sentences.en: Ryan Fisher was taking a lovely evening stroll down Sunset Boulevard in Los Angeles.
sentences.zh: 瑞安·费舍尔正漫步在洛杉矶的日落大道上，享受着美好的夜晚。

sentences.en: Fisher, a self-described nanny to a frenzy of Frenchies,
sentences.zh: 费舍尔自称是这群法斗的“保姆”，

sentences.en: had three French bulldogs in tow as he turned onto a residential street.
sentences.zh: 当时他正牵着三只法国斗牛犬转入一条住宅街道。

sentences.en: Suddenly, a white sedan pulled up next to him, and two men sprang out of the vehicle.
sentences.zh: 突然，一辆白色轿车停在他身边，两名男子从车里跳了出来。

sentences.en: They were armed, and they demanded that he hand over the dogs immediately.
sentences.zh: 他们持有武器，并要求他立即交出这些狗。

sentences.en: That is journalist Tova Danovich.
sentences.zh: 说话的是记者托娃·达诺维奇。

sentences.en: Ryan Fisher did not hand over the dogs, and as a result, he was shot once in the cheSt.
sentences.zh: 瑞安·费舍尔没有交出狗，结果胸部中了一枪。

sentences.en: Gunshots were heard, two of them.
sentences.zh: 枪声响起，一共两声。

sentences.en: The victim falls back as the assailants race back to the car with the two dogs.
sentences.zh: 受害者向后倒下，袭击者带着两只狗冲回车里。

sentences.en: And the attackers fled with two of the three Frenchies, who were named Koji and Gustav.
sentences.zh: 袭击者带着三只法斗中的两只逃跑了，它们的名字叫科吉和古斯塔夫。

sentences.en: Fisher luckily survived the shooting, but this dog-napping triggered a wave of media attention
sentences.zh: 费舍尔幸运地在枪击中幸存下来，但这次“劫狗”事件引发了媒体的广泛关注，

sentences.en: because Koji and Gustav weren't just any Frenchies.
sentences.zh: 因为科吉和古斯塔夫可不是普通的法斗。

sentences.en: They were Lady Gaga's Frenchies.
sentences.zh: 它们是Lady Gaga的法斗。

sentences.en: Friends of the man who was shot tell us he was constantly walking Lady Gaga's dogs in this neighborhood,
sentences.zh: 受害者的朋友告诉我们，他经常在这一带遛Lady Gaga的狗，

sentences.en: and he doesn't know if that was...
sentences.zh: 而他不知道这是否……

sentences.en: Due to their celebrity owner, a lot of people assumed the dogs were stolen to collect a ransom from Lady Gaga.
sentences.zh: 由于主人是名人，许多人认为这些狗被偷是为了向Lady Gaga勒索赎金。

sentences.en: She did, in fact, offer a $500,000 reward for their return, which is a lot of money.
sentences.zh: 事实上，她确实悬赏50万美元寻找它们的下落，这可是一大笔钱。

sentences.en: Yeah, that is a lot of money.
sentences.zh: 没错，那确实是一大笔钱。

sentences.en: But the truth is, if anyone had been walking down this road in Los Angeles with Frenchies
sentences.zh: 但事实是，如果当时有任何人在洛杉矶这条路上遛法斗，

sentences.en: at the time that this dog walker was, those dogs would have been targeted.
sentences.zh: 那么这些狗都会成为目标。

sentences.en: This whole fiasco had nothing to do with Lady Gaga.
sentences.zh: 整场闹剧与Lady Gaga毫无关系。

sentences.en: It was just a crime of opportunity.
sentences.zh: 这仅仅是一起随机犯罪。

sentences.en: Because at the end of the day, dogs aren't just pets.
sentences.zh: 因为归根结底，狗不仅仅是宠物。

sentences.en: They're commodities.
sentences.zh: 它们是商品。

sentences.en: And while this particular case got a huge amount of media attention,
sentences.zh: 虽然这起特定案件受到了媒体的大量关注，

sentences.en: French bulldog theft is actually extremely common.
sentences.zh: 但法国斗牛犬被盗其实非常普遍。

sentences.en: Frenchies can cost anywhere from $3,000 to $9,000.
sentences.zh: 法斗的价格从3000美元到9000美元不等。

sentences.en: And some with rare colored coat patterns go for up to $20,000.
sentences.zh: 而一些毛色罕见的品种甚至能卖到2万美元。

sentences.en: The average take in a bank robbery, by the way, according to the FBI, is $6,500.
sentences.zh: 顺便提一下，根据联邦调查局的数据，银行抢劫案的平均涉案金额为6500美元。

sentences.en: I'd wager that stealing someone's French bulldog off the street
sentences.zh: 我敢说，在街上偷走某人的法国斗牛犬，

sentences.en: is significantly easier than robbing a bank.
sentences.zh: 要比抢劫银行容易得多。

sentences.en: $15,000 worth of French bulldog is a pretty good day, I would say.
sentences.zh: 价值1.5万美元的法国斗牛犬，可以说是一笔相当不错的“收入”。

sentences.en: There is a huge demand for French bulldogs because these dogs are selectively bred and designed
sentences.zh: 市场对法国斗牛犬的需求巨大，因为这些狗是经过选择性繁育和设计的，

sentences.en: with human needs in mind.
sentences.zh: 充分考虑了人类的需求。

sentences.en: Frenchies are marketed as easy and friendly, perfect for millennial workers on the go.
sentences.zh: 法斗被营销为易于饲养且友好的品种，非常适合忙碌的千禧一代上班族。

sentences.en: They don't bark much or shed.
sentences.zh: 它们不怎么叫，也不怎么掉毛。

sentences.en: They barely need walks.
sentences.zh: 它们几乎不需要遛。

sentences.en: They're the second most popular dog breed in America today,
sentences.zh: 它们是当今美国第二受欢迎的犬种，

sentences.en: presumably because they don't have many of the needs or demands of regular dogs.
sentences.zh: 大概是因为它们没有普通狗那么多需求或麻烦。

sentences.en: But how did we get here, to this point where we've tried to breed the dog out of dogs?
sentences.zh: 但我们是怎么走到这一步的？走到试图通过繁育来消除狗的“狗性”这一步？

sentences.en: Tova Danovich wrote a great essay about the history of purebred dogs for Vox,
sentences.zh: 托娃·达诺维奇为Vox写了一篇关于纯种犬历史的精彩文章，

sentences.en: and she says that oddly enough, to understand the modern obsession with purebred dogs like the Frenchie,
sentences.zh: 她说奇怪的是，要理解现代人对法斗这类纯种犬的痴迷，

sentences.en: you actually have to start with chickens.
sentences.zh: 你其实得从鸡开始说起。

sentences.en: Victorian-era chickens.
sentences.zh: 维多利亚时代的鸡。

sentences.en: Someone brought Queen Victoria some extremely fancy chickens.
sentences.zh: 有人给维多利亚女王送了一些极其华丽的鸡。

sentences.en: And soon after receiving these very bougie chickens, the Queen became obsessed with owning poultry,
sentences.zh: 在收到这些非常时髦的鸡之后不久，女王就迷上了养禽，

sentences.en: which eventually meant everyone became obsessed with owning poultry.
sentences.zh: 这最终导致每个人都迷上了养禽。

sentences.en: Victorians never met a fad they didn't like, so...
sentences.zh: 维多利亚时代的人从不拒绝任何潮流，所以……

sentences.en: It became an international craze.
sentences.zh: 这变成了一种国际狂热。

sentences.en: These chickens would go for the equivalent of thousands of dollars and would be exhibited at poultry shows.
sentences.zh: 这些鸡的价格相当于数千美元，并且会在家禽展上展出。

sentences.en: They called it hen fever.
sentences.zh: 他们称之为“母鸡热”。

sentences.en: And it was because of all of these livestock shows and chicken shows that people were like,
sentences.zh: 正是因为所有这些牲畜展和家禽展，人们开始觉得，

sentences.en: you know what, we should also show dogs.
sentences.zh: 你知道吗，我们也应该展示狗。

sentences.en: And, you know, usually show that my dog is better than the dog that you have bred, specifically.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，通常是专门展示我的狗比你繁育的狗更好。

sentences.en: But how can you tell if my dog is better than your dog?
sentences.zh: 但你怎么能判断我的狗比你的狗好呢？

sentences.en: Today, we'd compare breeds.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们会比较品种。

sentences.en: But before the Victorian era, the term breed didn't actually exiSt.
sentences.zh: 但在维多利亚时代之前，“品种”这个词其实并不存在。

sentences.en: Instead, people used words like strain or variety to describe different types of dogs.
sentences.zh: 相反，人们使用“品系”或“变种”之类的词来描述不同类型的狗。

sentences.en: They were grouped according to the work they did.
sentences.zh: 它们是根据所从事的工作来分组的。

sentences.en: Herding and protecting.
sentences.zh: 牧羊和护卫。

sentences.en: Hunting and retrieving.
sentences.zh: 狩猎和寻回。

sentences.en: Pointing.
sentences.zh: 指示。

sentences.en: Guarding.
sentences.zh: 看守。

sentences.en: Sniffing.
sentences.zh: 嗅探。

sentences.en: And until the Victorian time, when we looked at dogs, we really looked at what purpose did they serve.
sentences.zh: 在维多利亚时代之前，当我们看狗时，我们真正看重的是它们发挥什么作用。

sentences.en: And the dog that served that purpose could look like just any number of different things.
sentences.zh: 而发挥那种作用的狗，外表可能千差万别。

sentences.en: It didn't really matter.
sentences.zh: 这并不重要。

sentences.en: Meaning there wasn't any concept of categorizing a dog based on what it looked like.
sentences.zh: 这意味着当时没有任何根据外貌对狗进行分类的概念。

sentences.en: It was all based around what it could do.
sentences.zh: 一切都基于它们能做什么。

sentences.en: Any dog that was good at fetching things was a retriever.
sentences.zh: 任何擅长衔取东西的狗都是寻回犬。

sentences.en: It didn't matter if it was big or small, slobbery, or hairless.
sentences.zh: 无论它是大是小，流口水还是没毛，都无所谓。

sentences.en: And then, in 1860, dog shows started popping up in England.
sentences.zh: 然后，在1860年，狗展开始在英国兴起。

sentences.en: And they were meant to determine the best dog.
sentences.zh: 它们的目的是评选出最好的狗。

sentences.en: But of course, it's really hard to prove my dog is the best at retrieving.
sentences.zh: 但当然，要证明我的狗最擅长寻回是非常困难的。

sentences.en: My dog is really good at finding rats in small holes.
sentences.zh: 我的狗非常擅长在小洞里找老鼠。

sentences.en: Skills like sniffing or retrieving are all kind of relative and hard to judge in competition.
sentences.zh: 嗅探或寻回之类的技能都是相对的，在比赛中很难评判。

sentences.en: So instead of that really kind of subjective way of going about things, they were like, you know, we'll make a standard that says a terrier should be 16 inches high,
sentences.zh: 所以，他们没有采用那种非常主观的方式，而是说，你知道，我们要制定一个标准，规定梗犬应该有16英寸高，

sentences.en: have this color fur, a tail that looks like this, this approximate body shape, because this is really easy to judge.
sentences.zh: 有这种颜色的毛，尾巴长这样，身体形状大概是这样，因为这非常容易评判。

sentences.en: A dog show was essentially a dog beauty contest with very strict guidelines.
sentences.zh: 狗展本质上是一场有着严格准则的狗狗选美比赛。

sentences.en: Judging was entirely based on a dog's visual appeal.
sentences.zh: 评判完全基于狗的视觉吸引力。

sentences.en: And because of these shows, dogs started to become categorized as breeds, which was much more than just a language change.
sentences.zh: 由于这些展览，狗开始被归类为“品种”，这不仅仅是语言上的改变。

sentences.en: Dog breeds were something entirely new, defined by their form and not their function.
sentences.zh: 犬种是一种全新的事物，由它们的外形而非功能来定义。

sentences.en: The different types of dogs became like blocks on a Pantone color card, each uniform and discreet.
sentences.zh: 不同类型的狗变得像潘通色卡上的色块一样，每个都统一且独立。

sentences.en: So it made it so people could compete with a wide range of dogs and say, my dog is the finest of all the dogs.
sentences.zh: 这使得人们可以用各种各样的狗来竞争，并说：我的狗是所有狗中最好的。

sentences.en: And that's really why that change happened.
sentences.zh: 这就是这种变化发生的原因。

sentences.en: This standardization of dog breeds was driven by a group of people in England called the Dog Fancy.
sentences.zh: 这种犬种标准化是由英国一群被称为“犬迷”的人推动的。

sentences.en: The Fancy were a loose group of urban working class Englishmen who bred and sold dogs.
sentences.zh: “犬迷”是一群松散的城市工人阶级英国人，他们繁育并出售狗。

sentences.en: And as you can imagine, the Fancy were interested in spectacle and show.
sentences.zh: 正如你可以想象的那样，犬迷们对奇观和表演很感兴趣。

sentences.en: But they had a problem.
sentences.zh: 但他们遇到了一个问题。

sentences.en: The Fancy felt like the judges at these dog shows were just giving the top prizes to their friends.
sentences.zh: 犬迷们觉得这些狗展的评委只是把最高奖项给了他们的朋友。

sentences.en: So they came up with a kind of rubric, a standardized set of points that would determine the best dog.
sentences.zh: 所以他们想出了一种评分标准，一套标准化的积分体系来决定哪只狗最好。

sentences.en: And for the first time ever, there were vigorous disagreements about the correct angle of an ear or the desired curl of a tail.
sentences.zh: 这是有史以来第一次，人们对耳朵的正确角度或尾巴的理想卷曲程度产生了激烈的争论。

sentences.en: And to develop a breed, all you really had to do was get a group of, you know, probably men together who wanted to breed dogs that all looked, you know, X way.
sentences.zh: 要开发一个品种，你真正需要做的就是召集一群人，你知道，大概是男人，他们想繁育出看起来都，你知道，是X样子的狗。

sentences.en: And say, OK, we have now made the Labrador Retriever.
sentences.zh: 然后说，好的，我们现在创造了拉布拉多寻回犬。

sentences.en: How wonderful.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: We've all decided that it should look in this specific way.
sentences.zh: 我们都决定它应该看起来是这个特定的样子。

sentences.en: So we are going to go to the local kennel club, apply for our dog to become, you know, a new breed, and the books will be closed.
sentences.zh: 所以我们要去当地的养犬俱乐部，申请让我们的狗成为，你知道，一个新品种，然后名册就会关闭。

sentences.en: Meaning once the Fancy had established a certain set of characteristics, that was the definition of the breed.
sentences.zh: 这意味着一旦犬迷们确定了一组特定的特征，这就是该品种的定义。

sentences.en: And what that means is if there were 30 dogs at that time that were considered Labrador Retrievers, there can never be any new Labrador Retriever added to that gene pool.
sentences.zh: 这意味着如果当时有30只狗被认为是拉布拉多寻回犬，那么这个基因库中就永远不能再增加新的拉布拉多寻回犬了。

sentences.en: And that is actually the definition of a purebred dog, is that it only comes from this group of genes when the books were closed.
sentences.zh: 这实际上就是纯种犬的定义，即它只来自名册关闭时那组基因。

sentences.en: It was the dog show that really defined the dog breeds we have today.
sentences.zh: 正是狗展真正定义了我们今天所拥有的犬种。

sentences.en: I think dog shows are really the reason for the transition from function to form.
sentences.zh: 我认为狗展确实是从功能向外形转变的原因。

sentences.en: So all of the changes that we've made to dog breeds, because the breed itself is a very visual standard, have been aesthetic choices.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们对犬种所做的所有改变，因为品种本身就是一个非常视觉化的标准，都是审美选择。

sentences.en: Throughout history, these dog breeds have been shifting and morphing based on aesthetic standards that change over time.
sentences.zh: 纵观历史，这些犬种一直在根据随时间变化的审美标准进行转变和演变。

sentences.en: Sometimes for no good reason other than personal taste.
sentences.zh: 有时仅仅是因为个人品味，没有其他正当理由。

sentences.en: The German Shepherd is a really great example of this, because the vast majority of German Shepherds today can trace their lineage back to the very first dog,
sentences.zh: 德国牧羊犬就是一个很好的例子，因为今天绝大多数德国牧羊犬都可以追溯到第一只狗，

sentences.en: known as the German Shepherd,
sentences.zh: 被称为德国牧羊犬，

sentences.en: who was named Horind von Grafath, which is fantastic.
sentences.zh: 它的名字叫霍兰德·冯·格拉法斯，这名字太棒了。

sentences.en: The breeders scoured different villages until they found Horind, and they bred him as the source of the original German Shepherd line, a dog breed specifically bred to herd sheep.
sentences.zh: 繁育者们搜遍了不同的村庄，直到找到霍兰德，他们以它为源头繁育了最初的德国牧羊犬品系，这是一种专门为牧羊而繁育的犬种。

sentences.en: If you looked at him compared to the German Shepherds that might be at Westminster Dog Show today, they're very, very different.
sentences.zh: 如果你把它和今天威斯敏斯特狗展上的德国牧羊犬相比，它们非常、非常不同。

sentences.en: That's because people's taste for what a German Shepherd should look like has changed since the first German Shepherd, again, I'm going to say his name, Horind von Grafath,
sentences.zh: 这是因为人们对德国牧羊犬应该长什么样的品味，自第一只德国牧羊犬——我再说一遍它的名字，霍兰德·冯·格拉法斯——

sentences.en: came on the scene.
sentences.zh: 出现以来就已经改变了。

sentences.en: It became a thing in the mid-century for German Shepherds to have a sloping back on them.
sentences.zh: 在世纪中叶，德国牧羊犬背部倾斜成为了一种潮流。

sentences.en: People began selecting for a sloping back, even though it hindered, you know, herding sheep, and was detrimental to the dog's health.
sentences.zh: 人们开始选择背部倾斜的特征，尽管这阻碍了，你知道，牧羊，并且对狗的健康有害。

sentences.en: And this was done for literally no practical reason, just because it looked cool.
sentences.zh: 这样做实际上没有任何实际原因，仅仅是因为它看起来很酷。

sentences.en: So over time, they've really changed from a dog that could herd sheep to one that, you know, maybe has trouble running because of the aesthetic choices that we've made.
sentences.zh: 所以随着时间的推移，它们确实从一种能牧羊的狗变成了一种，你知道，可能因为我们所做的审美选择而跑步困难的狗。

sentences.en: The governing aesthetics of dog shows trickled out to the masses, even when purebred owners never had any intention of breeding or showing dogs themselves.
sentences.zh: 狗展的统治性审美渗透到了大众之中，即使纯种犬主人从未打算自己繁育或展示狗。

sentences.en: And over time, breeds started to rise and fall in popularity, like fads.
sentences.zh: 随着时间的推移，品种的流行度开始像潮流一样起起落落。

sentences.en: Purebreds would become a proxy for class and social status.
sentences.zh: 纯种犬成为了阶级和社会地位的象征。

sentences.en: People started talking about how purebred dogs were, you know, really healthy and dignified and so classy and always well-behaved.
sentences.zh: 人们开始谈论纯种犬是多么，你知道，真正健康、尊严、优雅且总是表现良好。

sentences.en: And the dogs of the poor, those guys, who even knows what they're going to get up to.
sentences.zh: 而穷人的狗，那些家伙，谁知道它们会干出什么事来。

sentences.en: So that became a very, very quick class distinction.
sentences.zh: 所以这很快就变成了一种阶级区分。

sentences.en: That didn't really change until after the middle of the century.
sentences.zh: 这种情况直到世纪中叶之后才真正改变。

sentences.en: In the post-war era, purebred dogs were being bred on a much larger scale, like cars, guns, and sliced bread.
sentences.zh: 在战后时期，纯种犬的繁育规模要大得多，就像汽车、枪支和切片面包一样。

sentences.en: Dogs became another example of 20th century mass production.
sentences.zh: 狗成为了20世纪大规模生产的另一个例子。

sentences.en: Today, there is no question of the dog's place in society.
sentences.zh: 今天，狗在社会中的地位毋庸置疑。

sentences.en: He goes everywhere.
sentences.zh: 它无处不在。

sentences.en: A lot of farmers were kind of urged to treat dogs as like a side crop.
sentences.zh: 许多农民被敦促把狗当作副业来养。

sentences.en: Farmers in the Midwest were facing hard times with massive crop failures.
sentences.zh: 中西部的农民正面临着农作物大面积歉收的困境。

sentences.en: And the idea of breeding and selling purebred puppies started to seem like a foolproof way to make some extra cash on the side.
sentences.zh: 而繁育和出售纯种幼犬的想法，开始看起来像是一种赚取额外收入的万无一失的方法。

sentences.en: Plus, breeding dogs is much less labor-intensive than what it takes to grow food.
sentences.zh: 此外，繁育狗比种植粮食所需的劳动力要少得多。

sentences.en: The USDA even had a program promoting them.
sentences.zh: 美国农业部甚至有一个推广它们的项目。

sentences.en: American farmers started to pack dogs into chicken coops and rabbit hutches and sell puppies to pet stores.
sentences.zh: 美国农民开始把狗塞进鸡舍和兔笼里，并将幼犬卖给宠物店。

sentences.en: The supply of these purebred dogs exploded.
sentences.zh: 这些纯种犬的供应量爆炸式增长。

sentences.en: And with this newly booming retail pet industry, a lot of middle-class families could suddenly afford a purebred dog for the first time.
sentences.zh: 随着这个新兴的零售宠物产业的繁荣，许多中产阶级家庭突然第一次买得起纯种犬了。

sentences.en: But I think throughout history, we've really seen this same pattern play out where rich people did something and then people who were, you know,
sentences.zh: 但我认为纵观历史，我们确实看到了同样的模式在重演，富人做了某事，然后那些，你知道，

sentences.en: in a class slightly below them wanted to emulate that.
sentences.zh: 阶级稍低的人想要效仿。

sentences.en: Fast forward a couple of decades, and then we have TV and movies to help us determine which dogs we think of as cool and trendy.
sentences.zh: 快进几十年，我们有了电视和电影来帮助我们决定哪些狗是我们认为酷和时尚的。

sentences.en: So once television in particular became a really big medium, we started watching these dogs do really amazing things.
sentences.zh: 所以一旦电视成为一种非常重要的媒介，我们就开始观看这些狗做一些非常了不起的事情。

sentences.en: When I was a kid, the It dog was the Collie because of the Lassie movies and TV specials.
sentences.zh: 我小时候，最受欢迎的狗是柯利犬，因为《灵犬莱西》的电影和电视特辑。

sentences.en: For the generation before me, it was the German Shepherd because of Rin Tin Tin.
sentences.zh: 对于我上一代人来说，是德国牧羊犬，因为《丁丁历险记》里的那只狗。

sentences.en: When I was young, dating myself, we had wishbone.
sentences.zh: 我年轻的时候，暴露年龄了，我们有《威斯邦》。

sentences.en: So anyone with a Jack Russell Terrier was the coolest person in school.
sentences.zh: 所以任何养杰克罗素梗的人都是学校里最酷的人。

sentences.en: So we kind of get this idea implanted probably subconsciously that, hey, if I get one of these dogs, maybe it will also be amazing.
sentences.zh: 所以我们潜意识里被植入了一种想法，嘿，如果我养一只这样的狗，也许它也会很棒。

sentences.en: Remember 101 Dalmatians, that Disney animated movie based on a novel about 101 Dalmatians?
sentences.zh: 还记得迪士尼那部根据小说改编的动画电影《101忠狗》吗？

sentences.en: Well, after the movie came out in the 1960s, everyone wanted a Dalmatian.
sentences.zh: 好吧，在20世纪60年代电影上映后，每个人都想要一只大麦町犬。

sentences.en: And when they remade the film in the 90s...
sentences.zh: 当他们在90年代重拍这部电影时……

sentences.en: Something kind of interesting happened, which is that the same fad occurred.
sentences.zh: 发生了一件挺有意思的事，那就是同样的潮流又出现了。

sentences.en: People went out, bought a lot of Dalmatians.
sentences.zh: 人们纷纷出门，买了很多大麦町犬。

sentences.en: But people started noting that these Dalmatians were then winding up in animal shelters because people were buying their really cool spotted dogs.
sentences.zh: 但人们开始注意到，这些大麦町犬最终被送进了动物收容所，因为人们当初只是因为这些斑点狗看起来很酷才买的。

sentences.en: You had dogs who had much higher energy needs than were really appropriate for the families who were going out and buying these dogs.
sentences.zh: 这些狗的能量需求远高于那些购买它们的家庭所能提供的水平。

sentences.en: And it was a really huge problem.
sentences.zh: 这成了一个非常严重的问题。

sentences.en: It's such a problem, in fact, that people tend to refer to this rise and fall in dog popularity as the Dalmatian effect.
sentences.zh: 事实上，这个问题严重到人们倾向于将这种狗类流行度的起伏称为“大麦町效应”。

sentences.en: We see these cycles of it dogs going in and out of style throughout the years, certain breeds being sold and later abandoned.
sentences.zh: 多年来，我们一直看到这种流行犬种的更迭周期，某些品种被热销，随后又被遗弃。

sentences.en: And today, it seems like the apotheosis of all this is perhaps the French Bulldog.
sentences.zh: 而今天，这种现象的巅峰之作或许就是法国斗牛犬。

sentences.en: These dogs are everywhere, which makes sense because they're so damn cute.
sentences.zh: 这些狗随处可见，这很合理，因为它们实在太可爱了。

sentences.en: Frenchies in particular fall into a specific kind of lifestyle that they're really great for.
sentences.zh: 尤其是法斗，它们非常适合某种特定的生活方式。

sentences.en: And there is a reason why they're specifically very popular in cities like New York, Los Angeles, San Francisco,
sentences.zh: 它们在纽约、洛杉矶、旧金山等城市特别受欢迎是有原因的，

sentences.en: where there are a lot of wealthy people who maybe like to travel a lot.
sentences.zh: 因为那里有很多可能喜欢经常旅行的富人。

sentences.en: But these are dogs that are about 20 pounds.
sentences.zh: 但这些狗大约只有20磅重。

sentences.en: They are very small dogs, little tiny waist, giant head, big expressive eyes that kind of sit wide on their face.
sentences.zh: 它们是非常小的狗，腰部细小，头大如斗，大而富有表情的眼睛在脸上显得很宽。

sentences.en: They have this delightful smile, big bat ears.
sentences.zh: 它们有迷人的微笑和巨大的蝙蝠耳。

sentences.en: The way they vocalize, a lot of Frenchie owners describe it as talking because it's kind of a bit of a yodel, really, I think is the best way to describe it.
sentences.zh: 至于它们发声的方式，很多法斗主人形容那是在“说话”，因为那听起来有点像约德尔唱法，我觉得这是最好的描述方式。

sentences.en: Those endearingly large roly-poly heads mean they usually have to be borne by C-section.
sentences.zh: 它们那可爱的大脑袋意味着它们通常需要通过剖腹产出生。

sentences.en: The tiny little waist can cause a lot of spine deformities and nerve pain because they're so disproportionate.
sentences.zh: 细小的腰部会导致严重的脊柱畸形和神经痛，因为它们的身体比例太不协调了。

sentences.en: All those cute face wrinkles can make them prone to skin infections.
sentences.zh: 所有那些可爱的面部褶皱使它们容易患上皮肤感染。

sentences.en: And their squished faces lead to a lot of breathing probleMs.
sentences.zh: 而它们扁平的脸导致了许多呼吸问题。

sentences.en: They're not really good at exercising, so you don't have to feel bad for not taking them on long walks because especially on a hot day, it's really not good for them.
sentences.zh: 它们不太擅长运动，所以你不必因为没带它们长距离散步而感到内疚，因为特别是在炎热的天气里，这对它们真的不好。

sentences.en: So yeah, they're these cute little monstrosities of nature that because of all of these characteristics that have been bred into them, they're often really sick dogs.
sentences.zh: 所以没错，它们是自然界中可爱的小怪物，由于被刻意培育出的这些特征，它们往往是体质非常差的狗。

sentences.en: In a way, we are still breeding dogs for a purpose, like we were before the Victorians.
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，我们仍然像维多利亚时代之前那样，为了某种目的培育狗。

sentences.en: But the purpose has changed.
sentences.zh: 但目的已经变了。

sentences.en: It's not herding or hunting.
sentences.zh: 不再是为了放牧或狩猎。

sentences.en: It's to fit into the modern world.
sentences.zh: 而是为了适应现代世界。

sentences.en: Breeders will first sell you the idea of an easy dog, one that's hypoallergenic or small enough for your purse.
sentences.zh: 繁育者首先会向你推销“省心犬”的概念，比如低过敏性，或者小到能装进手提包。

sentences.en: And then the industry will sell you the stuff to go along with it, the timed feeders and water fountains,
sentences.zh: 然后行业会向你推销配套产品，比如定时喂食器和饮水机，

sentences.en: the motorized doggy doors for dogs to go in and out by themselves and pee on little patches of fake grass.
sentences.zh: 还有电动狗门，让狗能自己进出，在小块的人造草坪上排泄。

sentences.en: But it's gotten to the point where, as Tova says, we've broken the dog to accommodate us.
sentences.zh: 但正如托娃所说，情况已经到了我们为了迁就自己而“毁掉”了狗的地步。

sentences.en: After a century of breeding dogs for looks and not for health or talent,
sentences.zh: 经过一个世纪只看外表、不顾健康或能力的繁育，

sentences.en: a study in the 90s found that a quarter of all dog breeds recognized by the American Kennel Club suffered at least one genetic disorder.
sentences.zh: 90年代的一项研究发现，美国养犬俱乐部认可的所有犬种中，有四分之一至少患有一种遗传疾病。

sentences.en: The long list of degenerative conditions goes from German shepherds with bad hips to bull terriers that can spend 80% of their time uncontrollably chasing their own tails.
sentences.zh: 退行性疾病的名单很长，从髋关节发育不良的德国牧羊犬，到能花80%的时间无法控制地追逐自己尾巴的牛头梗。

sentences.en: Golden retrievers, for example, 60% of them get cancer, which is a huge issue.
sentences.zh: 例如金毛寻回犬，60%会患上癌症，这是一个巨大的问题。

sentences.en: And I think a lot of people getting that dog's, you know, that's not on the brochure when you're going to buy your dog.
sentences.zh: 我想很多人在买狗时，你知道，这并不在宣传册上。

sentences.en: And it's, I think a lot of people would still get them and love them anyway.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，很多人即便知道这一点，还是会买下并爱它们。

sentences.en: But I think it's really horrible to set people up without the information of this thing that they're buying into.
sentences.zh: 但我认为，在不告知消费者所购之物潜在风险的情况下就让他们入坑，这真的很糟糕。

sentences.en: But again, it's a matter of priorities.
sentences.zh: 但话说回来，这还是一个优先级的问题。

sentences.en: And getting rid of encephalitis in pugs and preserving the pug's cute, squished nose can be two conflicting priorities.
sentences.zh: 消除巴哥犬的脑炎和保留巴哥犬可爱、扁平的鼻子，可能是两个相互冲突的优先级。

sentences.en: Geneticists discovered that the mutation contributing to widespread deafness in Dalmatians is the exact same mutation that creates its signature spots.
sentences.zh: 遗传学家发现，导致大麦町犬普遍耳聋的突变，正是产生其标志性斑点的突变。

sentences.en: About 30% of Dalmatians end up losing their hearing.
sentences.zh: 大约30%的大麦町犬最终会失去听力。

sentences.en: But will people who want Dalmatians abide a Dalmatian without spots?
sentences.zh: 但那些想要大麦町犬的人会接受没有斑点的大麦町吗？

sentences.en: They're mongrels!
sentences.zh: 它们是杂种！

sentences.en: No spots!
sentences.zh: 没有斑点！

sentences.en: No spots at all!
sentences.zh: 一点斑点都没有！

sentences.en: What horrible little white rats!
sentences.zh: 多可怕的小白鼠啊！

sentences.en: There's a reason why we as humans obsess over breeds.
sentences.zh: 我们人类痴迷于品种是有原因的。

sentences.en: We don't have a lot of information available to us when we have to decide which dog to get.
sentences.zh: 当我们需要决定养哪种狗时，我们并没有太多可用的信息。

sentences.en: So we categorize dogs into breeds because it gives us a sense of predictability and control.
sentences.zh: 所以我们将狗分类为品种，因为它给了我们一种可预测性和控制感。

sentences.en: We're always putting, you know, people, things, feelings into categories.
sentences.zh: 我们总是把人、事物、感受归入各种类别。

sentences.en: It's a lot easier for us to understand the world in categories.
sentences.zh: 用类别来理解世界对我们来说容易得多。

sentences.en: And when you're getting a dog, you have this for-the-dog's-lifetime commitment of this creature from another species that you can't talk to that you're bringing in your house.
sentences.zh: 当你养狗时，你就要对这个来自另一个物种、无法交流、被你带进家门的生物承担起它一生的责任。

sentences.en: And in an ideal world, maybe you would, like, take some time to get to know each other firSt.
sentences.zh: 在理想的世界里，也许你会花点时间先互相了解一下。

sentences.en: But typically, you have to decide, I'm going to get this dog or I'm going to leave this dog behind within, you know, 30 minutes maybe when you meet them.
sentences.zh: 但通常情况下，你可能在见到它们后的30分钟内就得决定：要么养这只狗，要么放弃它。

sentences.en: And that's really tough.
sentences.zh: 这真的很艰难。

sentences.en: And sure, your Frenchie may be cute and apartment-friendly, like the brochure said.
sentences.zh: 当然，你的法斗可能像宣传册上说的那样可爱且适合公寓生活。

sentences.en: But, of course, not every French bulldog will be as advertised.
sentences.zh: 但当然，并非每只法斗都名副其实。

sentences.en: And not every owner is prepared for all the health issues that might come up over time.
sentences.zh: 而且并非每位主人都准备好应对随着时间推移可能出现的各种健康问题。

sentences.en: I think there are some people who are just not set up for even the most easygoing dog in the world.
sentences.zh: 我认为有些人甚至连世界上最随和的狗都养不好。

sentences.en: There are a lot of people who should maybe get an old dog and not a puppy.
sentences.zh: 有很多人或许应该养一只老狗，而不是幼犬。

sentences.en: And I think until we start talking about what, you know, breeds can and cannot guarantee, that's going to keep being a problem.
sentences.zh: 我认为在我们开始讨论品种能保证什么、不能保证什么之前，这个问题将持续存在。

sentences.en: There's a breeder in the Netherlands, Chantal van Kroening, who's experimenting with breeding a new kind of Frenchie.
sentences.zh: 荷兰有一位繁育者，尚塔尔·范·克罗宁，她正在尝试繁育一种新型法斗。

sentences.en: She's reshaping the French bulldog's smushed face to try to make it healthier.
sentences.zh: 她正在重塑法斗扁平的脸，试图让它们更健康。

sentences.en: Chantal's Frenchies have all the characteristics people love about these dogs, but they look distinctly different.
sentences.zh: 尚塔尔的法斗拥有人们喜爱这些狗的所有特征，但它们看起来明显不同。

sentences.en: They have a much longer neck and a longer nose.
sentences.zh: 它们的脖子更长，鼻子也更长。

sentences.en: These new Frenchies would hopefully have less genetic abnormalities.
sentences.zh: 这些新型法斗有望减少遗传异常。

sentences.en: These dogs wouldn't be accepted as Frenchies by the American Kennel Club, and they couldn't compete at dog shows.
sentences.zh: 这些狗不会被美国养犬俱乐部承认为法斗，也不能参加犬展。

sentences.en: But to the average consumer, it would hopefully mean their dogs can live longer.
sentences.zh: 但对于普通消费者来说，这意味着他们的狗有望活得更久。

sentences.en: From a consumer standpoint, I think people would be a lot happier with it, but it kind of goes against, like, the ethos of what the purebred dog is.
sentences.zh: 从消费者的角度来看，我认为人们会对此感到高兴得多，但这在某种程度上违背了纯种犬的精神。

sentences.en: Or maybe we should move on from the idea of breeds and think about dogs the way we did before Queen Victoria got those fancy chickens.
sentences.zh: 或者我们应该抛弃品种的概念，像维多利亚女王得到那些花哨的鸡之前那样看待狗。

sentences.en: The best thing to do isn't to look at dog breeds, but to actually return to those groups, like the herding group, terrier group.
sentences.zh: 最好的做法不是看犬种，而是回归到那些群体，比如牧羊犬组、梗犬组。

sentences.en: Because if you look within there, the traits do tend to be a little bit more accurate.
sentences.zh: 因为如果你深入观察，这些特征往往会准确一些。

sentences.en: You can kind of see, okay, does a terrier really fit my lifestyle when I have this beautiful garden and, you know, a fence that's very easy to dig under?
sentences.zh: 你可以看出，好吧，当我有一个漂亮的花园，而且栅栏很容易被挖开时，梗犬真的适合我的生活方式吗？

sentences.en: And that's going to tell you a lot more than any specific dog within that.
sentences.zh: 这比其中的任何特定品种更能告诉你答案。

sentences.en: We could just go back to classifying dogs by what they could do as dogs.
sentences.zh: 我们可以回到根据狗能做什么来对它们进行分类。

sentences.en: There'd still be some sense of the predictability that we crave.
sentences.zh: 这样依然会有我们渴望的那种可预测性。

sentences.en: It just wouldn't be based on looks.
sentences.zh: 只是不再基于外表。

sentences.en: I don't know if it's what I see as the future of purebred and designer dogs here,
sentences.zh: 我不知道这是否就是我所看到的纯种犬和设计师犬的未来，

sentences.en: but I would really like for that to happen.
sentences.zh: 但我真的很希望这种情况发生。

sentences.en: I think that we should not be breeding to a standard that necessitates the dog be unhealthy.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们不应该为了一个必须让狗不健康的“标准”去进行繁育。

sentences.en: That seems like a pretty, pretty easy shift to make from where I'm standing.
sentences.zh: 从我的角度来看，这似乎是一个非常、非常容易做出的改变。

sentences.en: The other easy shift is just to go to your local shelter and adopt a mutt.
sentences.zh: 另一个简单的改变就是去当地的收容所领养一只混种狗。

sentences.en: Because purebred or not, they're all good dogs.
sentences.zh: 因为无论是否纯种，它们都是好狗。

sentences.en: After the break, the creator of the Labradoodle says breeding this dog is his life's regret.
sentences.zh: 休息之后，拉布拉多贵宾犬的创造者说，繁育这种狗是他一生中最后悔的事。

sentences.en: After this, Buggle, Cockapoo, Schnoodle, Yorkie-poo, I'm sure you've come across these dogs before.
sentences.zh: 接下来，Buggle、Cockapoo、Schnoodle、Yorkie-poo，我相信你以前见过这些狗。

sentences.en: Dogs that are hybrid breeds made from two purebreds squished together with a cutesy portmanteau.
sentences.zh: 这些狗是由两种纯种犬拼凑在一起，并起了一个可爱合成词名字的杂交品种。

sentences.en: These dogs are often called designer dogs.
sentences.zh: 这些狗通常被称为“设计师犬”。

sentences.en: And perhaps the most notorious of all designer dogs is the Labradoodle.
sentences.zh: 而设计师犬中最臭名昭著的或许就是拉布拉多贵宾犬（Labradoodle）。

sentences.en: And that dog is what we consider to be the very first designer dog.
sentences.zh: 那只狗被我们认为是第一只设计师犬。

sentences.en: But the guy who created the first Labradoodle wonders whether he bred a designer dog or a disaster.
sentences.zh: 但创造了第一只拉布拉多贵宾犬的人却在怀疑，他繁育的是设计师犬还是灾难。

sentences.en: So in 1989, a man named Wally Conran was a breeder with a guide dogs for the blind type organization in Australia.
sentences.zh: 1989年，一个名叫沃利·康兰的人是澳大利亚一家导盲犬组织的繁育者。

sentences.en: Wally was contacted by a woman in Hawaii who was looking for a guide dog.
sentences.zh: 沃利接到了一位夏威夷女士的电话，她正在寻找一只导盲犬。

sentences.en: But she had a problem, which is that her husband was very allergic to the Labrador retrievers that are commonly used and trained to be guide dogs.
sentences.zh: 但她有一个问题，那就是她的丈夫对通常用于训练导盲犬的拉布拉多寻回犬严重过敏。

sentences.en: So Wally really wanted to solve this problem for the woman.
sentences.zh: 所以沃利真的很想为这位女士解决这个问题。

sentences.en: And his first thought was, I'll take poodles, which are known to be pretty low shedding, a little bit hypoallergenic, breed that to one of these Labrador retrievers.
sentences.zh: 他的第一个想法是，我用贵宾犬，因为它们以掉毛少、有点低过敏性而闻名，把它们和拉布拉多寻回犬杂交。

sentences.en: And maybe I'll find a dog that has the right temperament to be a guide dog, but isn't going to trigger these allergies in the same way.
sentences.zh: 也许我能找到一只既有导盲犬气质，又不会以同样方式引发过敏的狗。

sentences.en: So he finds these two dogs to breed, three puppies come out of the litter.
sentences.zh: 于是他找了两只狗进行繁育，一窝生了三只小狗。

sentences.en: He sends off hair samples from all of the dogs to Hawaii, and only one of them is actually not going to trigger this husband's allergies.
sentences.zh: 他把所有狗的毛发样本寄到了夏威夷，结果只有一只不会引发她丈夫的过敏。

sentences.en: So they get that puppy.
sentences.zh: 于是他们得到了那只小狗。

sentences.en: But Wally had a problem.
sentences.zh: 但沃利遇到了一个问题。

sentences.en: Two of the Labrador Poodle puppies weren't hypoallergenic, and he didn't know what to do with them.
sentences.zh: 另外两只拉布拉多贵宾犬并不具备低过敏性，他不知道该拿它们怎么办。

sentences.en: And despite the fact that the guide dogs program had a three to six month wait for guide dogs, when he called people on the list, they were like,
sentences.zh: 尽管导盲犬项目有三到六个月的等待期，但当他给名单上的人打电话时，他们的反应是：

sentences.en: we're going to wait for one of your normal dogs.
sentences.zh: “我们要等你的普通导盲犬。”

sentences.en: Thank you very much.
sentences.zh: “非常感谢。”

sentences.en: And he was so frustrated by this that he went to their PR department and was like, look, just tell the media we've bred a new special kind of dog.
sentences.zh: 他对此感到非常沮丧，于是他找到公关部门说，听着，告诉媒体我们繁育了一种新的特殊品种的狗。

sentences.en: It's called a Labradoodle.
sentences.zh: 它叫拉布拉多贵宾犬。

sentences.en: It was the exact same dog as the Labrador Poodle crossbreed, just with a different name.
sentences.zh: 这和之前的拉布拉多贵宾杂交犬是同一种狗，只是换了个名字。

sentences.en: It was a marketing gimmick that really caught on.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常成功的营销噱头。

sentences.en: The name stuck and people started to go wild for these dogs.
sentences.zh: 名字叫响了，人们开始为这些狗疯狂。

sentences.en: All of a sudden, he started getting all of these calls.
sentences.zh: 突然之间，他开始接到各种各样的电话。

sentences.en: Wally says he realized what he had done within a matter of days.
sentences.zh: 沃利说，他在几天之内就意识到自己做了什么。

sentences.en: He went to his boss and said, look, I've created a monster.
sentences.zh: 他去找老板说，听着，我创造了一个怪物。

sentences.en: We need to do something to control it.
sentences.zh: 我们需要采取措施来控制它。

sentences.en: But they couldn't put a patent on the breed and soon breeders from all over the world joined in on the trend.
sentences.zh: 但他们无法为这个品种申请专利，很快世界各地的繁育者都加入了这个潮流。

sentences.en: They became so popular that like every other time a dog becomes, you know, the dog, a lot of people started breeding these dogs together to make money.
sentences.zh: 它们变得如此受欢迎，以至于像其他任何时候某种狗成为“当红炸子鸡”一样，很多人开始为了赚钱而大量繁育这些狗。

sentences.en: And that, my friends, is how designer dogs first came on the scene.
sentences.zh: 朋友们，这就是设计师犬最初出现的方式。

sentences.en: That was 1989.
Today, Wally Conran is retired and he deeply regrets breeding that first Labradoodle.
sentences.zh: 今天，沃利·康兰已经退休，他深深后悔繁育了第一只拉布拉多贵宾犬。

sentences.en: He says he feels like he, quote, opened Pandora's box and, quote, released a Frankenstein.
sentences.zh: 他说他感觉自己“打开了潘多拉魔盒”，并“释放了一个科学怪人”。

sentences.en: That's because when a popular commodity collides with greed, things get ugly.
sentences.zh: 这是因为当热门商品与贪婪碰撞时，事情就会变得丑陋。

sentences.en: In this case, it means a lot of these dogs aren't carefully bred or that they're overbred and they end up with a whole host of health issues.
sentences.zh: 在这种情况下，这意味着许多狗没有经过精心繁育，或者被过度繁育，最终导致了一系列健康问题。

sentences.en: We had so much demand for dogs last year, in particular, that a lot of dogs have been actually coming in from overseas.
sentences.zh: 去年我们对狗的需求量特别大，以至于很多狗实际上是从海外运来的。

sentences.en: And those are marketed as, you know, the same dog.
sentences.zh: 而这些狗被当作同一种狗来销售。

sentences.en: You know, no one tells you that they're actually coming from the Ukraine.
sentences.zh: 你知道，没人会告诉你它们实际上来自乌克兰。

sentences.en: And a lot of these dogs are removed from their mothers younger than they're supposed to be.
sentences.zh: 而且许多小狗在比规定时间更早的时候就被从母亲身边带走了。

sentences.en: You know, vaccination records are falsified.
sentences.zh: 你知道，疫苗接种记录也是伪造的。

sentences.en: It's just any time you're turning a living animal into a commodity and then that commodity becomes popular, there are just snowballing problems that are going to come from that.
sentences.zh: 只要你把活生生的动物变成商品，而这种商品又变得流行，随之而来的问题就会像滚雪球一样越来越多。

sentences.en: Of course, a lot of people, Labradoodle owners included, would disagree that their dogs are the equivalent of Frankenstein's monster.
sentences.zh: 当然，很多人，包括拉布拉多贵宾犬的主人，会不同意他们的狗等同于科学怪人的怪物。

sentences.en: And it totally makes sense that they would.
sentences.zh: 这完全说得通。

sentences.en: The individual dogs are probably great.
sentences.zh: 这些个体狗可能很棒。

sentences.en: And if they're overall not as healthy, so be it.
sentences.zh: 如果它们整体上没那么健康，那就这样吧。

sentences.en: Your dog is great and it has a cute name.
sentences.zh: 你的狗很棒，而且名字很可爱。

sentences.en: How could you not love that?
sentences.zh: 你怎么能不爱呢？

sentences.en: But the dilemma is exactly the same as it is for purebred dogs.
sentences.zh: 但困境与纯种犬完全一样。

sentences.en: They just have a catchier name.
sentences.zh: 它们只是有一个更吸引人的名字而已。

sentences.en: 99% Invisible was produced this week by Lasha McDon and edited by Vivian Lay.
sentences.zh: 本周的《99% Invisible》由拉莎·麦克唐制作，维维安·莱剪辑。

sentences.en: Mix and tech production by Dara Hirsch.
sentences.zh: 混音和技术制作由达拉·赫什负责。

sentences.en: Music by our director of sound, Swan Rial.
sentences.zh: 音乐由我们的声音总监斯旺·里亚尔创作。

sentences.en: Delaney Hall is the executive producer.
sentences.zh: 德莱尼·霍尔担任执行制片人。

sentences.en: Kurt Kolstad is the digital director.
sentences.zh: 库尔特·科尔斯塔德担任数字总监。

sentences.en: The rest of the team includes Chris Berube, Christopher Johnson, Emmett Fitzgerald, Joe Rosenberg, Sophia Klatzker, and me, Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 团队其他成员包括克里斯·贝鲁贝、克里斯托弗·约翰逊、埃米特·菲茨杰拉德、乔·罗森伯格、索菲亚·克拉茨克，以及我，罗曼·马斯。

sentences.en: Special thanks to Tova Danovich.
sentences.zh: 特别感谢托娃·达诺维奇。

sentences.en: Check out her article, The Very Cute, Totally Disturbing Tale of the American It Dog on Vox.
sentences.zh: 请查看她在Vox上发表的文章《美国当红犬的可爱与令人不安的故事》。

sentences.en: And keep an eye out for Tova's forthcoming book about chickens.
sentences.zh: 也请留意托娃即将出版的关于鸡的书。

sentences.en: We are part of the Stitcher and SiriusXM podcast family, now headquartered six blocks north in the Pandora Building.
sentences.zh: 我们是Stitcher和SiriusXM播客家族的一员，现在总部位于北边六个街区的潘多拉大厦。

sentences.en: In beautiful, uptown, Oakland, California.
sentences.zh: 位于美丽的加利福尼亚州奥克兰市中心。

sentences.zh: 你可以在Facebook上找到我们的节目并参与讨论。

sentences.en: You can tweet at me, at Roman Mars, and the show at 99pi.org.
sentences.zh: 你可以在推特上关注我@RomanMars，以及节目@99pi.org。

sentences.en: We're on Instagram and Reddit too.
sentences.zh: 我们也在Instagram和Reddit上。

sentences.zh: 你可以在99pi.org找到我喜欢的其他Stitcher节目的链接，以及《99pi》的每一集往期节目。

sentences.zh: 好了，胡萝卜。

sentences.zh: 躺下。

sentences.en: Good boy, Carrot.
sentences.zh: 好孩子，胡萝卜。

sentences.zh: 说Stitcher。

sentences.en: Good.
sentences.zh: 很好。

sentences.zh: 说SiriusXM。
